pinyin: sān jūn yì dé, yī jiàng nán qiú
literal: three · armies · easy · get, one · general · hard · seek
natural: a thousand soldiers are easy to find, a good general is not

meaning.en: Ordinary people are plentiful but outstanding leaders are rare.
meaning.zh: 普通人好找，杰出的领导者难得。

equivalents: good leaders are hard to find
an army of sheep led by a lion

examples.zh: 三军易得，一将难求，公司最缺的是好领导。
examples.en: Soldiers are easy to find, generals are not; the firm lacks good leaders.

examples.zh: 三军易得，一将难求，招人容易，找接班人难。
examples.en: Hiring is easy, but finding a successor is hard.

usage.en: The variant begins 千军易得.
usage.zh: 也说“千军易得，一将难求”。

pinyin: yī jiàng wú néng, lèi sǐ sān jūn
literal: one · general · incompetent, exhaust · to death · three · armies
natural: an incompetent general wears out the whole army

meaning.en: An incapable leader makes everyone under him suffer.
meaning.zh: 领导无能，下面的人都跟着受累。

equivalents: a bad leader ruins the whole team
lions led by donkeys

examples.zh: 一将无能，累死三军，换个经理就好了。
examples.en: An incompetent leader wears everyone out; a new manager would help.

examples.zh: 项目一团糟，真是一将无能，累死三军。
examples.en: The project is a mess; the whole team suffers for one weak leader.

usage.en: Criticism of a poor leader; often used at work.
usage.zh: 批评无能的领导，常用于职场。

pinyin: jiǎo tù sǐ, zǒu gǒu pēng
literal: cunning · hare · dies, running · dog · is boiled
natural: when the cunning hare is dead, the hound is boiled

meaning.en: Once a useful person has served their purpose, they are discarded or killed.
meaning.zh: 事情成功后，功臣就被抛弃或杀掉。

equivalents: to be cast aside once one's work is done
to discard those who are no longer needed

examples.zh: 他帮老板打下天下，最后却被赶走，真是狡兔死，走狗烹。
examples.en: He built the firm for the boss, only to be pushed out: use and discard.

examples.zh: 狡兔死，走狗烹，功臣往往没有好下场。
examples.en: When the hare is dead the hound is cooked; the loyal rarely end well.

story.en: Fan Li, after helping Goujian of Yue defeat Wu, warned Wen Zhong: 'When the swift birds are gone the good bow is stored; when the cunning hare is dead the hound is boiled.'
story.zh: 范蠡劝文种：“蜚鸟尽，良弓藏；狡兔死，走狗烹。”

usage.en: Often paired with 飞鸟尽，良弓藏; stresses ingratitude of rulers or bosses.
usage.zh: 常与“飞鸟尽，良弓藏”并用，指上位者忘恩负义。

pinyin: bǎo hàn bù zhī è hàn jī
literal: full · man · not · know · hungry · man's · hunger
natural: the well-fed cannot understand the hunger of the starving

meaning.en: Those who are comfortable cannot understand the hardship of the poor.
meaning.zh: 生活安逸的人体会不到穷人的苦处。

equivalents: the well-fed don't know the hungry's pain
how the other half lives

examples.zh: 饱汉不知饿汉饥，他怎么会懂我们的难处。
examples.en: The well-fed don't know hunger; how would he understand our difficulties?

examples.zh: 饱汉不知饿汉饥，有钱人很难体会穷人的艰辛。
examples.en: The rich can hardly feel the poor's hardship.

usage.en: Often a complaint against the privileged.
usage.zh: 多用来抱怨衣食无忧的人不理解疾苦。

text: 穷在闹市无人问，富在深山有远亲
pinyin: qióng zài nào shì wú rén wèn, fù zài shēn shān yǒu yuǎn qīn
literal: poor · in · busy · market · no · one · asks, rich · in · deep · mountain · has · distant · kin
natural: a poor man in a busy market is ignored; a rich man in the mountains has distant relatives

meaning.en: People ignore you when you are poor and flatter you when you are rich.
meaning.zh: 穷时无人理睬，富了远亲也来巴结。

equivalents: fair-weather friends
everybody loves a rich man

examples.zh: 穷在闹市无人问，富在深山有远亲，他深有体会。
examples.en: He knows from experience that the poor are ignored and the rich have friends.

examples.zh: 中奖后，亲戚们纷纷上门，真是穷在闹市无人问，富在深山有远亲。
examples.en: After the lottery win, relatives came flocking.

usage.en: A cynical comment on human nature.
usage.zh: 感叹世态炎凉。

pinyin: qióng rén de hái zi zǎo dāng jiā
literal: poor · people's · children · early · run · household
natural: children of the poor take charge of the household early

meaning.en: Children from poor families mature early and learn to take responsibility.
meaning.zh: 穷人家的孩子很早就懂事，担起家庭责任。

equivalents: hardship makes children grow up fast

examples.zh: 穷人的孩子早当家，他十岁就会做饭了。
examples.en: Poor children grow up early; he could cook at ten.

examples.zh: 她从小帮家里干活，真是穷人的孩子早当家。
examples.en: She helped at home from a young age.

usage.en: Positive, often used with sympathy and respect.
usage.zh: 多含同情与敬意。

pinyin: fù bù guò sān dài
literal: wealth · not · exceed · three · generations
natural: riches do not last beyond three generations

meaning.en: Family fortunes rarely last long; the heirs tend to squander them.
meaning.zh: 家业很难传过三代，子孙往往败光。

equivalents: from clogs to clogs in three generations
shirtsleeves to shirtsleeves in three generations

examples.zh: 富不过三代，这家公司传到孙辈就衰落了。
examples.en: Wealth rarely lasts three generations; the firm declined under the grandchildren.

examples.zh: 富不过三代，要教育孩子勤俭。
examples.en: Riches rarely survive three generations, so teach children thrift.

usage.en: Often used of family firms and heirs.
usage.zh: 常用于家族企业和富二代。

pinyin: fù guì xiǎn zhōng qiú
literal: wealth · rank · risk · in · seek
natural: wealth and status are sought through risk

meaning.en: Great rewards come only from taking risks.
meaning.zh: 要想得到大富贵，必须冒风险。

equivalents: nothing ventured, nothing gained
no risk, no reward

examples.zh: 富贵险中求，他放弃稳定工作去创业。
examples.en: No risk, no reward: he gave up a stable job to start a business.

examples.zh: 富贵险中求，但也要量力而行。
examples.en: Fortune favours risk, but know your limits.

usage.en: Encourages risk-taking; may also warn of recklessness.
usage.zh: 既鼓励冒险，也可能提醒鲁莽。

synonyms: 撑死胆大的，饿死胆小的

pinyin: rén qióng zhì duǎn, mǎ shòu máo cháng
literal: person · poor · ambition · short, horse · thin · hair · long
natural: a poor man's ambitions shrink, as a thin horse's coat grows long

meaning.en: Poverty wears down one's confidence and ambition.
meaning.zh: 人一穷就缺乏志气，没有远大追求。

equivalents: poverty crushes ambition

examples.zh: 人穷志短，马瘦毛长，他不敢再有什么想法。
examples.en: Poverty shrinks one's ambition; he no longer dares to dream.

examples.zh: 人穷志短，马瘦毛长，但也有人穷志不穷。
examples.en: Poverty shortens ambition, but some stay ambitious though poor.

usage.en: Often quoted with sympathy, or contrasted with 人穷志不穷.
usage.zh: 常与“人穷志不穷”对比。

text: 马善被人骑，人善被人欺
pinyin: mǎ shàn bèi rén qí, rén shàn bèi rén qī
literal: horse · gentle · is · by people · ridden, person · gentle · is · by people · bullied
natural: a gentle horse is ridden, a gentle man is bullied

meaning.en: Being too meek invites others to push you around.
meaning.zh: 太老实善良就会被人欺负。

equivalents: nice guys finish last
if you're a doormat, people walk on you

examples.zh: 马善被人骑，人善被人欺，该硬气时就要硬气。
examples.en: Gentle horses get ridden and gentle people bullied; be firm when needed.

examples.zh: 他总是忍让，结果马善被人骑，人善被人欺。
examples.en: He always gave way and was walked over.

usage.en: Advice to be assertive.
usage.zh: 劝人该强硬时要强硬。

pinyin: tù zi jí le yě yǎo rén
literal: rabbit · anxious · even · bite · people
natural: even a cornered rabbit will bite

meaning.en: Even the meekest will fight back when pushed too far.
meaning.zh: 再老实的人被逼急了也会反抗。

equivalents: even a worm will turn
a cornered rat fights

examples.zh: 别逼他太紧，兔子急了也咬人。
examples.en: Don't push him too hard; even a rabbit bites when cornered.

examples.zh: 兔子急了也咬人，何况是人。
examples.en: If a cornered rabbit bites, so will a person.

usage.en: A warning to those who bully the weak.
usage.zh: 多用来警告欺压弱者的人。

synonyms: 老虎不发威，你当我是病猫
antonyms: 马善被人骑，人善被人欺

pinyin: gǒu gǎi bù liǎo chī shǐ
literal: dog · change · cannot · eat · dung
natural: a dog can't stop eating dung

meaning.en: Bad habits and a bad nature never change.
meaning.zh: 恶习和本性很难改变。

equivalents: a leopard can't change its spots
you can't teach an old dog new tricks

examples.zh: 他出狱没多久又去赌博，真是狗改不了吃屎。
examples.en: Not long out of prison he's gambling again: a leopard can't change its spots.

examples.zh: 别指望他改，狗改不了吃屎。
examples.en: Don't expect him to change.

usage.en: Vulgar; used about incorrigible people.
usage.zh: 较粗俗，指本性难移的人。

pinyin: gǒu zuǐ lǐ tǔ bù chū xiàng yá
literal: dog · mouth · in · spit · not · out · ivory
natural: you can't get ivory out of a dog's mouth

meaning.en: A nasty person cannot say anything nice.
meaning.zh: 坏人说不出好话。

equivalents: you can't expect good words from a bad man
a foul mouth speaks no good

examples.zh: 别理他，狗嘴里吐不出象牙。
examples.en: Ignore him; nothing nice ever comes out of his mouth.

examples.zh: 她骂人的话太难听了，真是狗嘴里吐不出象牙。
examples.en: What she said was so offensive.

usage.en: Rude; used as an insult toward a person who talks nastily.
usage.zh: 粗话，用于骂人说话难听。

pinyin: gǒu yǎn kàn rén dī
literal: dog · eyes · look · people · low
natural: with a dog's eyes, looking down on people

meaning.en: To look down on others, especially because of their wealth or rank.
meaning.zh: 瞧不起人，以貌取人，势利。

equivalents: to look down one's nose at people
to be a snob

examples.zh: 这家店的店员狗眼看人低，见我穿得普通就爱答不理。
examples.en: The shop assistants look down on people; they ignored me as I was dressed plainly.

examples.zh: 别狗眼看人低，说不定他以后比你强。
examples.en: Don't look down on people; he may surpass you.

usage.en: Rude; describes snobbery.
usage.zh: 粗俗说法，指势利眼。

synonyms: 门缝里看人——把人看扁了
有钱人家的看门狗——势利眼

pinyin: huì yǎo rén de gǒu bù jiào
literal: can · bite · people · 's · dog · not · bark
natural: the dog that really bites doesn't bark

meaning.en: Truly dangerous people do not make a fuss; loud ones are often harmless.
meaning.zh: 真正厉害的人不声张，喊得凶的反而不可怕。

equivalents: barking dogs seldom bite
still waters run deep

examples.zh: 会咬人的狗不叫，要小心那个安静的对手。
examples.en: The dog that bites doesn't bark; beware of the quiet rival.

examples.zh: 会咬人的狗不叫，别小看沉默的人。
examples.en: Don't underestimate the silent ones.

usage.en: A caution about quiet but dangerous people.
usage.zh: 提醒小心沉默的厉害角色。

text: 不管黑猫白猫，能捉到老鼠就是好猫
pinyin: bù guǎn hēi māo bái māo, néng zhuō dào lǎo shǔ jiù shì hǎo māo
variants: 不管白猫黑猫，捉住老鼠就是好猫
不管黄猫黑猫，只要捉住老鼠就是好猫
literal: no matter · black · cat · white · cat, can · catch · mouse · is · good · cat
natural: it doesn't matter whether the cat is black or white, as long as it catches mice

meaning.en: Judge methods by results, not by labels or ideology.
meaning.zh: 不论方法如何，能解决问题就是好办法。

equivalents: the proof of the pudding is in the eating
whatever works

examples.zh: 不管黑猫白猫，能捉到老鼠就是好猫，先把事情做成再说。
examples.en: Whatever works: let's get it done first.

examples.zh: 他用人只看能力，不管黑猫白猫，能捉到老鼠就是好猫。
examples.en: He hires on ability alone: a good cat is one that catches mice.

usage.en: Popularly linked with Deng Xiaoping's 1960s remark; often shortened to 黑猫白猫论.
usage.zh: 与邓小平的言论联系紧密，常简称“黑猫白猫论”。

pinyin: niú bù hē shuǐ qiǎng àn tóu
literal: ox · not · drink · water · force · press · head
natural: force the ox's head down when it won't drink

meaning.en: To force someone to do something they do not want to do.
meaning.zh: 别人不愿意，硬要强迫。

equivalents: you can lead a horse to water but you can't make it drink

examples.zh: 他不想去，你也别牛不喝水强按头。
examples.en: He doesn't want to go; don't force him.

examples.zh: 学习得靠自觉，牛不喝水强按头没有用。
examples.en: Studying must be voluntary; forcing doesn't work.

usage.en: Often a plea against forcing someone's will.
usage.zh: 常用来劝人不要强迫。

pinyin: hǎo mǎ pèi hǎo ān
literal: good · horse · match · good · saddle
natural: a good horse deserves a good saddle

meaning.en: Good people or things deserve suitable accessories; also used of well-matched pairs.
meaning.zh: 好东西要有好的配件，好人要配好搭档。

equivalents: a fine horse needs a fine saddle
clothes make the man

examples.zh: 好马配好鞍，这么好的手机该配个好壳。
examples.en: A good horse needs a good saddle; such a phone deserves a good case.

examples.zh: 好马配好鞍，新郎新娘真是天生一对。
examples.en: A good horse and a good saddle: the couple are perfectly matched.

usage.en: Often used in wedding compliments or about matching quality.
usage.zh: 常用于称赞般配，也可指搭配得当。

text: 羊肉没吃着，惹了一身膻
pinyin: yáng ròu méi chī zháo, rě le yī shēn shān
literal: mutton · not · eat · get, attract · one · body · gamey smell
natural: never got to eat the mutton, but ended up smelling of it

meaning.en: To get blamed or tainted without having gained any benefit.
meaning.zh: 好处没捞到，反而惹了一身麻烦。

equivalents: to get the blame without the benefit
all the trouble and none of the gain

examples.zh: 这事我根本没赚钱，羊肉没吃着，惹了一身膻。
examples.en: I made no money from this, only trouble.

examples.zh: 羊肉没吃着，惹了一身膻，他后悔参与了这件事。
examples.en: He regretted getting involved: all trouble and no gain.

usage.en: Used about being dragged into trouble for nothing.
usage.zh: 指白白惹上麻烦。

pinyin: féi shuǐ bù liú wài rén tián
literal: rich · water · not · flow · outside · people's · fields
natural: fertile water should not flow into outsiders' fields

meaning.en: Keep good things within the family or group rather than giving them to outsiders.
meaning.zh: 好处要留给自己人，不让外人占便宜。

equivalents: charity begins at home
keep it in the family

examples.zh: 这个项目交给自家公司做，肥水不流外人田。
examples.en: Give the project to our own company; keep it in the family.

examples.zh: 肥水不流外人田，有好机会先考虑亲戚。
examples.en: Keep opportunities in the family; consider relatives first.

usage.en: Neutral but can imply favouritism or nepotism.
usage.zh: 中性，但可能含任人唯亲之意。

synonyms: 自留地里撒尿——肥水不落外人田

pinyin: xīn guān shàng rèn sān bǎ huǒ
literal: new · official · take · post · three · fires
natural: a new official lights three fires on taking office

meaning.en: A new leader starts with energetic reforms to establish authority.
meaning.zh: 新领导刚上任，往往要推行几项新措施。

equivalents: a new broom sweeps clean

examples.zh: 新官上任三把火，新经理一来就改了考勤制度。
examples.en: A new broom sweeps clean: the new manager changed the attendance rules at once.

examples.zh: 新官上任三把火，大家等着看他怎么烧。
examples.en: Everyone waits to see what the new boss will do.

usage.en: Neutral; sometimes with the hint that the zeal won't last.
usage.zh: 中性，有时暗示热度不会持久。

pinyin: pá de gāo, shuāi de zhòng
literal: climb · high, fall · hard
natural: the higher you climb, the harder you fall

meaning.en: The greater your rise, the more severe the fall.
meaning.zh: 爬得越高，摔下来越惨。

equivalents: the bigger they are, the harder they fall
pride comes before a fall

examples.zh: 爬得高，摔得重，贪官一旦被查就一无所有。
examples.en: The higher they climb, the harder they fall; corrupt officials lose everything.

examples.zh: 他从巅峰跌落，真是爬得高，摔得重。
examples.en: He fell from the peak: the higher you climb, the harder the fall.

usage.en: A warning to the ambitious and arrogant.
usage.zh: 用来警告得意的人。

pinyin: zhàn de gāo, kàn de yuǎn
literal: stand · high, see · far
natural: the higher you stand, the farther you see

meaning.en: A higher position or broader perspective brings greater foresight.
meaning.zh: 站得高才能看得远，视野更开阔。

equivalents: a high vantage point gives a wider view
think big picture

examples.zh: 站得高，看得远，管理者要有全局观。
examples.en: The higher you stand the farther you see; managers need to see the whole picture.

examples.zh: 登上山顶，才懂什么叫站得高，看得远。
examples.en: Standing on the summit shows what it means to see far.

usage.en: Both literal and metaphorical; often paired with 登高望远.
usage.zh: 既指实际登高，也比喻眼界。

synonyms: 不畏浮云遮望眼，自缘身在最高层
